corpus.title: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
corpus.signal_text:
Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
- Published
Ukraine's President Volodymr Zelensky has condemned Donald Trump's announcement of a deal to import Russian diesel into the US.
Zelensky called it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".
Trump said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately "to the American and global marketplace" followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.
It is understood the US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April as part of the deal, but other assets like those in American banks are still frozen.
In his Truth Social post, Trump added that a further three million tonnes of Russian diesel would be delivered "within a short period", dependent on the condition of its refineries, which have been attacked by Ukraine.
Putin later said Russia, which introduced a ban on diesel exports earlier this year, was willing to supply both the US and global markets with oil and petroleum products, but his statement did not specify amounts.
In a post on social media, Zelensky said Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".
"We count on America's fair support for our defence of life, for our defence of people in Ukraine â and on the United States having a correspondingly strong conversation with Russia. A strong one, not a weak one," he wrote.
Analysts, however, have questioned whether Russia is capable of providing that quantity of diesel and the extent to which doing so will ease prices for American consumers.
- Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices 
  - Published14 hours ago
Tim Armitage, investment strategist at Quilter Cheviot, said the numbers mentioned by Trump were "relatively small".
He said the first tranche equated to approximately 2.25 million barrels, and daily US consumption was around 3.8 million barrels, "so it won't make a material difference to pump prices in the US".
"Granted, there are then two more releases to come, but it does appear to be a slightly desperate move by President Trump to try to lower inflation ahead of the midterms."
The BBC has asked the White House what Russia will get from the US in return for the commitment.

corpus.title: Trump Announces Deal with Putin to Deliver Russian Diesel to U.S.
corpus.signal_text:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that Russia has agreed to supply millions of tons of diesel fuel to the American and global market, following a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The president said the first shipments would begin immediately, with larger deliveries scheduled through November and beyond in a post on Truth Social.
Trump laid out a delivery schedule that escalates over time:
I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter.
The president said Russia would then deliver up to 3,000,000 additional tons, depending on the condition of its refineries.
He tied the arrangement to U.S. leverage in the Persian Gulf, where American forces have operated throughout the war with Iran.
“Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump wrote.
Trump named lower prices for American farmers, ranchers, and truckers as his priority and closed the announcement with a line on Tehran.
“Iran will not have a Nuclear Weapon!” Trump added.
The announcement follows the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which the president signed into law last month. The statute takes effect Oct. 19, directs tariffs of up to 500 percent on Russian goods, and allows secondary sanctions on countries that purchase Russian fuel.
Many of the law’s provisions can be waived by the president.
Trump imposed major oil sanctions on Russia last October but issued waivers this year, citing disruptions from the Iran conflict that drove up energy costs and inflation.
The deal lands as diesel sits near a record of roughly $6.50 a gallon weeks before the November midterms. Last week, Trump said Europe had agreed to release diesel reserves “immediately,” and days later he signed an order expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel at a rally in Nebraska.

corpus.title: ‘We’re being used as a front,’ Zelensky says of Trump’s diesel deal with Putin
corpus.signal_text:
Russia and the U.S. have agreed on a deal to supply Russian diesel fuel to the U.S. and global markets. President Donald Trump announced the agreement on the evening of October 9 after a phone call with Vladimir Putin. Trump called the talks “highly successful.” Putin confirmed that Russia is ready to supply oil and petroleum products to the U.S. and global markets.
The U.S. said it is easing sanctions on Russian diesel. The Treasury Department has already issued a temporary license allowing sales of Russian diesel on the global market through April 7, 2027, despite U.S. sanctions. Washington previously eased sanctions on Russian oil temporarily because of a market crisis caused by the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran.
Russia has also begun lifting restrictions on diesel exports, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said. Sanctions and domestic export bans restrict exports of Russian oil and petroleum products worldwide. A ban on diesel and marine fuel exports by producers, for example, remains in effect through the end of October. Russia imposed it amid Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and a domestic fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian attacks over the summer.
Trump said the two sides agreed on the “immediate” delivery of more than 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel. Russia will supply another 500,000 metric tons in November, followed by an additional million metric tons. Novak said Russia is ready to supply additional diesel to the U.S. market as early as October. Exports are also expected to rise in November and December as refineries resume operations after repairs.
Ukraine criticized the diesel deal between Moscow and Washington. President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media that any easing of sanctions on Russia without agreements on de-escalation shows “obvious weakness.” “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis,” he said.
The deal comes as talks on ending the war resume. A Ukrainian delegation is reportedly meeting with U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Miami on October 9 and 10. Reuters reported that the national security advisers of the U.K., France, and Germany, along with representatives of NATO and the EU, were invited to the talks. Axios repo

corpus.title: Germany Sticks to Russia Sanctions After Trump Diesel Announcement
corpus.signal_text:
Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine following United States President Donald Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted U.S. sanctions on Russian fuel.
"The federal government has taken note of the U.S. decision relating to Russian diesel deliveries," government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said in a statement.
He said Germany's position remained clear: "The federal government remains committed to the decisions on sanctions against Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions."
He said Germany's support for Ukraine was unchanged and diplomatic efforts to reach a solution would continue.
Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. He said his administration temporarily lifted U.S. sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine.
Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, have risen to near record levels, posing a risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who visited Kyiv last weekend, has said repeatedly that Germany, Ukraine's largest European donor, would not reduce its support for the Kyiv government.

corpus.title: Trump Makes Deal With Putin On Diesel Exports. Ukraine Calls It A 'Gift'
corpus.signal_text:
WASHINGTON -- US President Donald Trump said he reached an agreement with President Vladimir Putin to temporarily ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports, a move Ukraine immediately criticized as a "gift" to the Kremlin.
Seeking to contain soaring energy prices, Trump said in a social media post on October 9 that the two leaders agreed to release 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tons in November and another million after that.
The move will see prices "COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote.
Diesel futures fell about 4 percent after the announcement but remained more than 110 percent higher than at the start of the year. Brent crude traded at around $104 a barrel, down just 0.3 percent on the day.
The decision came as Ukrainian, US, and European officials held talks in Miami aimed at ending Russia’s war against Ukraine. The discussions concluded without a breakthrough.
The waiver drew critical comments from Kyiv to lawmakers in Washington, who warned that easing restrictions could provide Moscow with additional revenue to sustain its war against Ukraine.
It also raised questions about US policy toward Russia following Trump’s recent signing of legislation intended to tighten sanctions against countries supporting Moscow’s energy trade.
"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote in a post on social media.
"Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis."
To enable the flow of diesel, the US Treasury Department issued a temporary general license authorizing the sale, delivery, and import of Russian-origin diesel fuel through April 7, 2027.
Trump said that after the initial flows, Russia would supply a further 3 million tons “within a short period of time.”
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Moscow was ready to increase supplies in October, with exports expected to rise in November and December as refineries resume operations after maintenance.
Diesel prices have climbed since the United States and Israel launched air strikes on Iran in February, sparking a conflict that is now in its eighth month.
